title: Eczema (Atopic Dermatitis)
subtitle: A chronic inflammatory skin condition causing itchy, dry, red, and cracked skin. It commonly starts in childhood but can affect people of all ages.

sections.title: Symptoms
sections.intro: Eczema affects about 10-20% of children and 1-3% of adults worldwide. While it cannot be cured, most people can manage their symptoms effectively with proper skincare and trigger avoidance.
items: Intense itching, especially at night
Dry, cracked, scaly skin patches
Red to brownish-grey patches on hands, feet, ankles, wrists, neck
Small, raised bumps that may weep fluid and crust
Thickened, leathery skin from scratching (lichenification)
Raw, swollen skin from scratching

sections.title: Causes
sections.intro: Eczema results from a combination of genetic and environmental factors that impair the skin barrier and dysregulate the immune response.
items: Gene mutations affecting the skin barrier protein filaggrin
Overactive immune response to environmental triggers
Family history of eczema, hay fever, or asthma
Environmental triggers, soap, detergent, pollen, pet dander
Stress and sweating can trigger flare-ups
Food allergies (in some cases), eggs, peanuts, dairy

sections.title: Prevention
items: Moisturise skin twice daily with fragrance-free emollient
Identify and avoid personal triggers
Use mild, fragrance-free soaps and detergents
Keep fingernails short to prevent skin damage from scratching
Wear loose, soft, breathable clothing
Keep indoor humidity moderate (45-55%)

sections.title: Treatment
items: Topical corticosteroids, first-line treatment for flares
Topical calcineurin inhibitors (Tacrolimus) for sensitive areas
Dupilumab (Dupixent), biologic for moderate-severe eczema
Antihistamines for itching (sedating at night)
Wet wrap therapy for severe flares
Antibiotics if skin is infected from scratching

facts: Impaired barrier allows allergens and irritants to penetrate
